fog_veil._comment: P2-002 (visual-claude lane, 2026-10-12). The catalogue found that a freshly entered realm's map was an empty dark canvas: undiscovered fog is opaque, so at 0% surveyed there are no terrain or road relationships between the named destinations. With this enabled, undiscovered cells in the full map (tab_map.gd) are a dark veil at undiscovered_alpha, so the baked terrain and roads show dimly beneath it and surveyed ground still reads as revealed. Landmarks, labels, discovery, saves and the minimap are unchanged. PRESENTATION ONLY. Stays OFF until a code-blind PASS.
fog_veil._why_round2: Round 1 code-blind judge: WEAK. A 0.5 veil showed blurry terrain and no routes, and it overrides the deliberate opaque fog (tab_map.gd FOG_UNDISCOVERED note: the map 'does not reveal everything automatically'). Round 2 keeps the fog opaque (undiscovered_alpha 1.0) and instead draws the authored road network above it (roads_above_fog), per UX.md: 'The map begins with Grandpa's Village and roads revealed.' Meadows, Stormwood (spurs to hidden pockets excluded) and Cloudreach (ground routes only); Tidewake has no route polylines the tab can read.
fog_veil._comment_sea_lanes: P2-002 Tidewake (UI lane, 21 Oct 2026): Tidewake had no road polylines, so its map stayed markers on fog. With sea_lanes on, each island's authored land spine/circuit draws as a road and the main-path sheltered crossings draw as dashed sea lanes, from water_world.json. Presentation only; OFF until a code-blind PASS.
fog_veil._comment_painted_chart: P2-002 GPU pass (UI lane, 22 Oct 2026): the map read as a black canvas (GPU 1.83). painted_chart paints surveyed ground as a shaded chart from the realm's own heights in the chapter palette; cloud_fog keeps unsurveyed cells fully opaque (OW3: the map never reveals unexplored terrain) but draws them as cloud cover in the realm's tone, with a soft edge at the survey line. Presentation only; OFF until a code-blind pass.

_comment: Map behaviour tunables that are NOT authored places. data/config/map_landmarks.json stays the place table (landmarks, regions, starting reveal); this file holds the rules the map applies to the world it is drawing. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_local_label_candidate: Device-local F42 presentation: existing margin placement starts at 16x after paired1080/720 map review and controller/consumer proofs. Region names leave the revealed village road clear. No fog, discovery, input, save or peer change. Opt-in --map-label-margin-candidate remains equivalent to this shipping gate.
_comment_local_labels: At the closest village scale, visible discovered region names sit in the panel margin so they do not cover nearby roads and buildings. This is device-local presentation; it reveals no terrain or destination.
_comment_initial_zoom: A first map open shows nearby surveyed terrain around the trainer rather than fitting the 8 km corridor into a narrow strip. LT still reaches the whole-realm overview, and the player's chosen zoom is remembered across tab opens. This changes no fog, discovery, save payload or peer state.
_comment_alpha_pin: CL-W1, owner directive D-0904B-1 plus its same-day amendment A-3: 'Within 300 m an alpha appears on the map, and does not disappear until caught' -- amended to 'caught OR beaten', which is what makes the pin actionable for a player whose five slots are already full. 16 alpha/elder clusters are authored across data/config/bands/*/spawns.json and were, until this landed, entirely unadvertised: the player could walk past every one of them and never know. The pin is placed from the AUTHORED cluster centre, not from a live body -- at 300 m the body is very often not streamed in yet, and a pin that only appears once you can already see the creature advertises nothing.

alpha_pin._comment_radius_m: The owner's number, verbatim. Measured on the XZ plane only (height is ignored): the corridor climbs and a 3D distance would pin a ridge alpha later than a flat-ground one at the same map distance, which is not what a player reading a map means by 'within 300 m'.
alpha_pin._comment_check_interval_s: Matches game_state.gd's own fog/landmark discovery cadence. 16 XZ distance comparisons is nothing, but running them every frame would still be 16 needless comparisons a frame for the whole chapter, and a 300 m radius cannot be crossed inside half a second on foot or mounted.
alpha_pin.first_pin_message: An alpha is near — marked on your map.
alpha_pin._comment_first_pin_message: Shown once per save, on the FIRST pin ever placed, through game_state.gd's push_world_message(). Once the player knows what the mark means, repeating the sentence at every one of the remaining 15 is nagging -- the mark appearing on the map is itself the notification from then on.

_comment_realm_link: OP-0905-27 (docs/owner/OWNER_PLAYTEST_2026-09-05.md): 'the map should show all the regions you've uncovered so meadows and clouds together.' scripts/ui/tab_map.gd's realm selector lets the full map show EITHER realm's own fog/regions/landmarks; this marker is the crossing between them, drawn on whichever realm is showing, pointing at the other. Positions are read straight from data/config/realm_transitions.json (`meadows_cloudreach_gate`) and data/config/cloudreach_world.json (`transition_points.meadows_entry`) -- the single shared source those files' own headers already name for this exact handoff -- so nothing here duplicates a coordinate that could drift out of step with the real gate. This block only says how the marker LOOKS and what unlocks it.

realm_link._comment_icon: assets/ui/icons/map/gate.png. CLAUDE.md forbids new Meadows art; the vendored gate icon already reads as a threshold/crossing and needed no new generation.
realm_link._comment_marker_size: A touch larger than a 'major' landmark's 38px (tab_map.gd's own `_marker_size`) -- this is the one marker on the map that changes which REALM you are looking at, not just where you are within one.
realm_link._comment_marker_colour: UITokens.TEAL spelled out as a literal hex string -- this file has no access to that autoload's constants. Deliberately the same teal family the player's own marker already uses (tab_map.gd's PLAYER ring/arrow), so the crossing reads as 'a way you personally can go', not a third HUD colour.
realm_link._comment_unlock_flags: Cloudreach counts as reachable on the Meadows map the moment ANY of these progression flags is set (docs/decisions/D110: the Warden grants `realm_key_cloudreach` at the same beat as `legendary_freed`; `cloudreach_chapter_started` additionally covers a save that reached Cloudreach through the debug teleport rather than the story gate). tab_map.gd also treats the player physically standing in Cloudreach, or that realm's own MapState already holding any discovery, as unlocked -- those are live facts, not flags, and stay in code rather than duplicated here. An empty list here falls back to this same default in code.
realm_link._comment_labels: What the crossing marker is captioned, keyed by which map is CURRENTLY showing -- i.e. the label names the destination, not the realm you are looking at.
